application_guidance.input_pattern: Exp-concave proper full-information OCO with Euclidean comparator movement and sufficiently small path budget.
read_original_when: Using parameter-explicit constants, finite precision, anytime horizons or conditional spectral acceleration.
sensitive_conditions: The learner adapts to unknown P_T but the displayed curved formula has a path-window condition.
Full all-path ensemble evaluates multiple bases; its gradient count differs.
Exact real-arithmetic projection model does not by itself imply polynomial bit complexity.

content.intended_use: Use the curved learner in its stated path window, with its actual arithmetic and feedback requirements.

dependencies: Imported source interfaces: Lemmas B.1–B.12 and Theorem B.16, with locators above
map: B.1 proves regret domination and lambda-exp-concavity of the common rank-one surrogate. B.2–B.3 give O(log T) surviving starts and prefix master overhead a=lambda^(-1)log((T+1)(K+1)).
B.4–B.6 give feasibility correction, Gaussian mixability and lambda r_t<=F_t(u_t)-F_{t+1}(u_t), with F_t(u)=KL(N(u,tau^2 I)||P_t).
B.7 makes sqrt(F) Lipschitz in u with coefficient 1/(sqrt(2)tau). B.8 shifts energy by cumulative surrogate excess plus drawdown threshold H, controlling movement while every prefix exceeds -H.

B.9 recursively selects a fresh history in the first half of each interval. Negative prefixes pay restart costs. After deleting bad nodes, each remaining component has at most L=ceil(log_2(T+1)) good nodes. This yields unconditional low-variation interval cost H_tau/64.
B.10 partitions the comparator path into at most 1+P_T/V_tau intervals. B.11 adds Gaussian smoothing error gamma tau^2||g_t||^2/2, with no extra dimension trace factor.

B.12 handles dyadic discretization and both scale endpoints. B.16 obtains clipped all-path bound C{(d+1)Lambda_T^2/gamma+min_{tau in [D/T,D]}[sqrt(d+1)Lambda_T^2 P_T/(gamma tau)+gamma G^2 T tau^2]} capped by GDT. For P_T<=c gamma^2 G^2 T D^3/(sqrt(d+1)Lambda_T^2), balancing gives the curved rate. Fixed D,G,eta yield Theorem 4.1.
B.2 counts O(log^2 T) states, charging one dense spectral computation and exact projection per state. The faster primitive must include eigenbasis change and reconstruction.

proofs.reading_coverage: Read statements and associated proof portions in original PDF pp.13–23; checked displayed Theorem 4.1 and Algorithm 1 on attached pp.6–7.

assumptions: Euclidean diameter of W is at most D>0. Each f_t is differentiable convex, eta-exp-concave with eta>0, and ||grad f_t(w)||_2<=G for every w in W, with G>0.
D,G,eta are fixed independently of d,T. Learner may know d,T,D,G,eta,W but not the comparator or P_T.
Full-information protocol: predict before loss revelation, then evaluate its gradient at the prediction.
For every a in R^d and A positive definite an oracle returns an exact minimizer of (w-a)^T A(w-a) over W, at arithmetic cost C_proj(d). Dense eigendecomposition and reconstruction cost O(d^3).
statement.conclusion: Reg_T(u)<=C[d Lambda_T^2+d^(1/3) Lambda_T^(4/3) T^(1/3) P_T(u)^(2/3)]. The learner uses one gradient at its actual prediction per round, O(log^2(2T)) Gaussian states, O((d^3+C_proj(d))log^2(2T)) arithmetic operations per round, and O(d^2 log^2(2T)) stored real numbers. If a separate primitive performs the complete rank-one precision update, covariance flooring AND reconstruction in original coordinates in O(d^2), the d^3 term can be replaced by d^2.
statement.objects_and_definitions: For positive integers d,T, W subset R^d is nonempty compact convex. Reg_T(u)=sum_t[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u_t)] and P_T(u)=sum_{t=2}^T||u_t-u_{t-1}||_2 for u in W^T. Define Lambda_T=1+log(2T), gamma=min{eta/2,1/(4GD)}, lambda=gamma/2. An eta-exp-concave loss satisfies concavity of exp(-eta f) on W.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist positive constants c,C depending only on D,G,eta such that the proper SparseGauss predictions satisfy the conclusion for every realized admissible loss sequence and every comparator path in the specified window. No probabilistic success qualifier.

witness_interface.grid_and_schedule: K=floor(log_2 T), tau_k=D 2^(-k), q_k=1/(K+1). Lifetime ell(i)=2^(nu_2(i)+2); active starts S_t={i<=t:t-i<=ell(i)}. Each active pair (i,k) stores one Gaussian initialized at birth to N(w_0,D^2 I), w_0 in W.
witness_interface.master: Initial p_1^(1,k)=q_k. Predict weighted mean of active history means. Update weights by exp(-lambda tilde f_t(x_t^(i,k))). Before t+1 give total 1/(t+1) to the newborn start split by q_k, multiply surviving old weights by t/(t+1), delete expired starts and renormalize. Each history applies equations (21)–(25).
witness_interface.surrogate: After predicting w_t use g_t=grad f_t(w_t) and tilde f_t(v)=<g_t,v-w_t>+(gamma/2)<g_t,v-w_t>^2. All histories reuse this gradient.
